name: tui-tailscale
tagline: Self-hosted Tailscale from the terminal: the control plane and this node
description:
Self-hosted Tailscale from the terminal, both ends of it: the [Headscale](https://headscale.net) control plane on this host, and this machine as a tailnet node.

The node screens show the state, login server, addresses and routes, and the peers. `j` joins (this host's own control plane offered first), with an optional pre-auth key that never touches a command line; each setting is one `tailscale set`.

The control-plane screens list headscale's users, nodes and pre-auth keys under a panel showing what `/etc/headscale/config.yaml` says, with one line naming the next missing step. `S` sets the transport, `server_url` and `dns.base_domain`; `O` the identity provider (Google or any OIDC), its secret written to a root-only file; `F` fixes file ownership; `r` approves advertised routes. Each change to config.yaml is a minimal diff, confirmed, then a restart.

When `tailscale` or `headscale` is absent, `i` installs it. `--demo` shows every screen with nothing installed.

screenshots.caption: The node screen: state, login server, addresses, and the settings that decide what this node routes
The peers screen: owner, address, state, exit node offers and the subnets each peer serves
The control plane: the readiness line, what config.yaml says, and the headscale users
The control plane's nodes: owner, state and routes, the pending one spelled out for the selected router
Approving a node's advertised routes: what is approved and what is revoked, previewed
A join previewed: the pre-auth key file, IP forwarding, tailscale up and the key file's removal, in one dialog
A join without a key: the login URL on a line of its own, outside the frame, whole, ready to copy
Picking an exit node from the peers that offer one
The help screen, generated from the action table

keys.action: Switch screen (node, peers, and headscale's users, nodes, preauth keys)
Join a tailnet: login server (this host's control plane offered), key, hostname, routes
Toggle accepting routes / edit the advertised subnet routes
Pick the exit node to use / toggle offering this node as one
Install tailscale (node screens) or headscale (control-plane screens) when absent
Create a headscale user (users screen) or pre-auth key (keys screen)
Control plane (users screen): server and transport / OIDC provider (Google, generic)
Fix ownership of headscale's state, secret and backup files (users screen)
Approve / revoke a node's advertised routes (subnet router, exit node)
Expire / rename / delete the selected headscale node
Reload (ctrl+r on the control plane's nodes screen, where r is routes)

notes.impact: `preauthkeys list` requires a `--user`, so the pre-auth keys screen may be empty; users and nodes are unaffected

source.command:
git clone https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-tailscale
cd tui-tailscale && make demo

pacman.note: Available once the first release lands in pkgs.tui.tools.

apt.note: Available once the first release lands in pkgs.tui.tools.

dnf.note: Available once the first release lands in pkgs.tui.tools.

binary.command:
curl -fsSL https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-tailscale/releases/download/v{version}/tui-tailscale_{version}_linux_{arch}.tar.gz | tar -xz tui-tailscale
sudo install -m0755 tui-tailscale /usr/local/bin/tui-tailscale

security.needs_sudo: Every change escalates, previewed first: tailscale up/set/down/logout, the key file under /run, IP forwarding, headscale's CLI, config.yaml, the OIDC secret file, its unit and the installs. The node is read as you; headscale's socket and config are root-only.
security.no_network_note: No connection of its own. On demand, previewed: the installs (i) fetch Tailscale's repository files or the tui-tools key (pinned fingerprint); O and --check --probe-issuer fetch the IdP's public discovery document, unprivileged.
